title: Certificate verify record — /certs/{cert_id}.json
description:
The public verify record for one certificate, regenerated on issue and on every status change (FS08-060). This shape is BYTE-AUTHORITATIVE: the public verify route is a passthrough and no consumer may rename or reshape a field — same names (`cid`, `typ`, `variant`), structured `scope`, `band` with no currency prefix (FS08-060a). The record never contains more subject data than the certificate itself displays (CERT-026), individual-subject records are unlisted (unguessable ULID, excluded from every index and sitemap, served `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, CERT-060), and the route reads this artifact only — never a database (FS08-061).

`ct: null` means signed-but-not-yet-logged, and the verify page renders UNVERIFIED (CERT-030). Clients can independently re-derive inclusion from the published log segments. Erasure leaves a tombstone: `status: "revoked"` with the subject fields removed, hash-only log entries retained (CERT-045/031).

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`. The enum widens additively when the P-M3 producer takes a value of its own.

status.description: CERT-040. `expired` is clock-derived from `period.validUntil` and needs no write; expiry is non-destructive and verifies as 'was valid for period P' (CERT-041).

sub.description: Display name. ABSENT on a tombstoned record after an erasure request (CERT-045).

band.description: Corporate types only; no currency prefix.

ct.description: Transparency-log position, computed at publish against the log segments. NULL for a signed-but-unlogged certificate — which the verify page must render as UNVERIFIED, not as a warning (CERT-030, FS10-041).

revocation.description: Present when `status` is `revoked`. Verify pages render the class LABEL only — no free-text shaming (FS08-064).

ctRef.description: Hash of the revocation log entry, which itself references the original entry's hash (CERT-033).

coverageWindow.description: For a waiver-derived certificate whose waiver was revoked: the ORIGINAL coverage window is retained alongside the revocation date, because revocation is prospective and the historical window remains true (CERT-042, FS08-066).

jws.description: The compact JWS — the certificate itself. Present so a client can validate the signature offline against a JWKS copy without a second fetch (CERT-025).

kid.description: Frozen key-id scheme `psn-{env}-{yyyy}-{n}` (FS08-101). A prod route refuses sandbox key material outright (FS08-103).

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).
